title: A different gate
paragraphs: Daniel reached the airport two hours before his flight. His boarding pass said Gate 12, so he bought a sandwich near that gate. While he was eating, he received a message from his sister. She asked him to buy a small gift at the airport store. Daniel checked the time and decided that he had enough time.

The store was only five minutes away. He chose a book and waited to pay. Just then, he heard an announcement about his flight. It was leaving from Gate 20 instead of Gate 12. The departure time had not changed. Daniel left the book on a shelf and walked quickly to the new gate. A staff member checked his passport there. He boarded with the last group of passengers and sent his sister a message: the gift would have to wait until his next visit.

questions.question: Why did Daniel go to the store?
options: His gate was inside the store
His sister asked for a gift
questions.evidence: She asked him to buy a small gift at the airport store.
questions.explanation: Wizyta w sklepie wynikała z prośby siostry.

questions.question: What changed about the flight?
questions.evidence: It was leaving from Gate 20 instead of Gate 12.
questions.explanation: Zmieniła się bramka, nie godzina odlotu.

questions.question: Did Daniel buy the book?
options: No, the store had no books
No, he left it before paying
Yes, he paid at the gate
questions.evidence: Daniel left the book on a shelf and walked quickly to the new gate.
questions.explanation: Zostawił książkę, żeby dotrzeć do nowej bramki.

questions.question: What happened in the end?
options: He caught the flight without a gift
questions.evidence: He boarded with the last group of passengers
questions.explanation: Zdążył wejść na pokład, ale nie kupił prezentu.

title: The table by the window
paragraphs: Ruby booked a table for six people at a restaurant. She asked for a table by the window because her grandfather liked watching the river. When they arrived, the waiter showed them a table in the middle of the room. Ruby explained what she had requested. The waiter checked the booking and apologized. The window table was ready, but it had only five chairs.

Ruby's cousin was not coming because she was ill, so there were only five people in the group. They moved to the window table and ordered lunch. Ruby's grandfather chose fish, but the waiter said it would take twenty minutes longer than the other meals. He chose pasta instead. Nobody was in a hurry, but he wanted to eat with everyone else. After lunch, the family took a photo by the river. Ruby sent it to her cousin with a message: they would visit again together.

questions.question: Why did Ruby want a window table?
options: The middle of the room was closed
Her grandfather liked the river view
questions.evidence: her grandfather liked watching the river.
questions.explanation: Prośba dotyczyła widoku, a nie ceny czy zamkniętej sali.

questions.question: Why were five chairs enough?
options: A child stood by the window
questions.evidence: Ruby's cousin was not coming because she was ill
questions.explanation: Rezerwacja była dla sześciu osób, lecz przyszło pięć.

questions.question: Why did the grandfather choose pasta?
options: He wanted to eat with the others
The waiter brought the wrong dish
questions.evidence: he wanted to eat with everyone else.
questions.explanation: Nie brak czasu, lecz wspólny posiłek zdecydował o zmianie zamówienia.

questions.question: Who received the photo?
questions.evidence: Ruby sent it to her cousin
questions.explanation: Kuzynka nie uczestniczyła w obiedzie, więc dostała zdjęcie.

title: A useful mistake
paragraphs: On Tuesday, Omar rode his bike to work. Near the park, he heard a strange sound from the back wheel. He stopped and called a repair shop. The mechanic said she could look at the bike that afternoon. Omar locked it outside a cafe and took the bus to his office.

At lunchtime, he realized that he had given the mechanic the wrong street name. He called again and corrected it. The mechanic laughed and said there were two cafes with the same name in town. She had not left the shop yet, so the mistake did not waste her journey. Later, she collected the bike and repaired it. Omar picked it up after work. The repair cost less than he expected because the wheel did not need replacing. He saved the shop's number in his phone and wrote down the correct address of the cafe too.

questions.question: How did Omar finish his journey to work?
questions.evidence: took the bus to his office.
questions.explanation: Rower zostawił pod kawiarnią; do pracy pojechał autobusem.

questions.question: What information did he correct?
questions.evidence: he had given the mechanic the wrong street name.
questions.explanation: Pomyłka dotyczyła ulicy, na której stał rower.

questions.question: Why did the mistake not waste a journey?
options: The mechanic was still at the shop
questions.evidence: She had not left the shop yet
questions.explanation: Mechanik jeszcze nie wyjechała, kiedy dostała poprawny adres.

questions.question: Why was the bill lower than expected?
options: Only the bus ticket cost money
questions.evidence: the wheel did not need replacing.
questions.explanation: Naprawa nie wymagała zakupu nowego koła.

title: The earlier appointment
paragraphs: Clara had an appointment at a clinic on Friday afternoon. On Thursday, the receptionist called and offered her a time that morning instead. Another patient had canceled. Clara agreed because she wanted to ask the doctor about a cough before a weekend trip. She told her manager that she would arrive at work late.

At the clinic, Clara waited beside a man who was reading a newspaper. He had arrived before her, but the nurse called Clara first. The man was waiting for a different doctor. Clara's doctor examined her and told her to rest. He did not say that she needed to cancel her trip, but he suggested avoiding long walks. Clara and her friend had planned a full day in the mountains. They changed that plan and booked a quiet place near a lake. Clara was glad she had accepted the earlier appointment: now she had time to organize a gentler weekend.

questions.question: Why could Clara see the doctor earlier?
options: The clinic opened a new building
Her friend gave her an appointment
questions.evidence: Another patient had canceled.
questions.explanation: Zwolnił się termin innego pacjenta.

questions.question: Why was Clara called before the man?
questions.evidence: The man was waiting for a different doctor.
questions.explanation: Kolejność przyjścia nie rozstrzygała, bo czekali do różnych lekarzy.

questions.question: What did the doctor suggest?
questions.evidence: he suggested avoiding long walks.
questions.explanation: Zalecił mniej wysiłku, ale nie nakazał odwołania wyjazdu.

questions.question: How did Clara change her weekend?
options: She moved the trip to Friday
She went alone to the mountains
questions.evidence: booked a quiet place near a lake.
questions.explanation: Zmieniła charakter wypoczynku, a nie zrezygnowała z niego.

title: The note on the fridge
paragraphs: Three students shared an apartment. Every Sunday, they wrote a shopping list on the fridge. This week, Nina added milk and apples. Josh added bread. Amir saw the list on Monday morning and bought all three things on his way home from class. He put the receipt beside the list so they could share the cost.

That evening, Nina came home with another bag of apples. She had seen a message from Josh about buying bread, but she had not checked the fridge. At first, she thought Amir had forgotten to tell everyone about his shopping. Then she noticed his message in their group chat. Her phone had been turned off during class. They now had too many apples, but nobody was angry. Amir suggested making a cake. After dinner, they agreed on a new rule: the person who finished the shopping would cross the items off the list as well as send a message.

questions.question: Who bought everything on the list?
questions.evidence: Amir saw the list on Monday morning and bought all three things
questions.explanation: Amir kupił mleko, jabłka i chleb.

questions.question: Why did Nina miss Amir's message?
options: He sent it the next day
Amir sent it to Josh only
questions.evidence: Her phone had been turned off during class.
questions.explanation: Wiadomość została wysłana; Nina jej nie widziała z powodu wyłączonego telefonu.

questions.question: What did they have too much of?
questions.evidence: They now had too many apples
questions.explanation: Nina kupiła dodatkowe jabłka.

questions.question: What was the new rule?
options: Update both the list and the chat
questions.evidence: cross the items off the list as well as send a message.
questions.explanation: Nowa zasada łączy dwie czynności, a nie zastępuje wiadomości samą listą.
